Implemented vimanam #45 diff subcommand (design option b) on branch feat/diff stacked on PR #91: src/diff.rs (Node grammar state machine threaded through diff_values, severity rule table, Deltas), utils::resolve_schema_value/canonicalize_schema_value (depth counted per $ref hop, cap 64), exit code 3 for --fail-on-breaking, --report deltas. Review found two real bugs (depth cap counted JSON levels so 9+ hop changes were silently dropped; keyword-lookalike property names misclassified), both fixed and amended. 75 unit + 100 integration tests green. User asked to stop after this round. [Resource] (score 6.78)

vimanam #45 diff: user chose design option (b), JSON-canonicalisation diff (resolve $refs into serde_json::Value, canonicalise, generic Value differ with JSON-pointer paths, rule table classifies schema changes breaking/non-breaking, unmatched -> Review), over the cheaper option (c) fingerprint-only MVP. Why: field-level schema detail is what makes drift behind a shared $ref actionable and lets --fail-on-breaking cover schema changes. Implemented on stacked branch feat/diff on top of feat/completions-hygiene-stats (PR #91). [Logic] (score 6.06)

Each feature went implementation agent -> review agent -> remediation agent (amend). All CI gates green locally: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 32 unit + 86 integration tests.

vimanam #67/#68 design confirmed 2026-09-05: in-memory Vec<Page> site model (option a) for multi-file output, and #68 skill tree as a SiteLayout preset over it. One tweak recommended over the design doc: use a dedicated --out-dir flag rather than overloading -o to mean a directory when --split is set.

CI is a timing adversary local gates are not: a race with a microsecond window on a dev machine is a real defect on a loaded runner. Anything inserted into serve startup must re-verify the pre-handshake durability test's assumptions — and that test's matcher ('session attached') matches both the memory-level and serve-level log lines, which is how the widened window was caught.
